newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst's Celanese sells sulphur business.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst's Celanese sells sulphur business.

text.p: Celanese GmbH, a unit of German chemicals group Hoechst AG, said on Tuesday that it planned to sell its inorganic sulphur chemicals business to Grillo-Werke AG of Duisberg.
The sulphur chemicals business is based at Hoechst in Frankfurt and has annual sales of 50 million marks and around 100 employees.

Grillo-Werke is a family-owned company founded 155 years ago, which makes and sells sulphur dioxide and sulphuric acid. The group employs around 1,000 people and has annual sales of 350 million marks.
In a statement, Grillo-Werke said that it plans to continue to operate and expand the sulphur operations on a long-term basis at the Hoechst site and that the relevant employees will be taken over.
